key_insight: CAHR reconstructs detector error models by turning syndrome statistics into a globally consistent discrete hypergraph, avoiding the false positives common in greedy inference.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum error-correction engineers a more reliable way to identify circuit-level noise structure before tuning decoders and mitigation strategies.
method: Solve exact algebraic correlation equations from syndrome data.
Use a top-down concurrent-pruning scheme to remove incompatible candidate mechanisms.
Separate inference into topology recovery first, then continuous probability fitting.
evidence_signal: In benchmark tests, CAHR recovered the fault topology without false positives for both d=5 rotated surface codes and dense 8-body 2D color codes.
watch_item: Exact continuous parameter estimation may still be limited in dense codes by a variance cascade, so topology recovery does not fully remove statistical uncertainty in probabilities.
paper_title: Reconstruction of detector error model for quantum error correction
